study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) benign simple descriptors (BDs)
Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (ADNEX) model
outcome: Natural history of adnexal masses (resolution, complications, surgical intervention)
Specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value, positive predictive value of the two-step strategy
cohort: The cohort consisted of 291 women with an adnexal mass identified on ultrasonography during pregnancy between 2017 and 2022 at Queen Charlotte's and Chelsea Hospital, London, UK, with 267 followed up to the postnatal period.
finding: The two-step strategy using BDs and the ADNEX model had a specificity of 90.2% and sensitivity of 63.6% for classifying adnexal masses, suggesting that BDs apply to most adnexal masses during pregnancy and many can be managed expectantly.
mod_finding: Four (1.5%) women underwent surgical intervention electively during Cesarean section, indicating one mode of surgical management for adnexal masses during pregnancy.
followup_time: Up to the postnatal period (first postnatal ultrasound scan)
gest_age: Median gestational age of 12 (IQR, 8-17) weeks at adnexal mass identification
